title: POC: PII mapping, benchmarking & retention plan with Redwood
next_steps: Redwood to share PII mapping template and sample retention matrix
Customer to provide anonymized workload sample (5000 requests) for benching
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run next Tue and share results within 3 business days
action_items: Lena Park: Send PII mapping template and SSO/KMS checklist by 2027-12-12
Tom Becker: Export 5k anonymized requests and upload link to shared drive by 2027-12-14
Marco Ruiz: Prepare benchmark script and default perf config and run test on dedicated pool during pilot window (owner: Marco) by 2027-12-16
summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on how Clearwave will handle PII in prompts/attachments during a 3-week pilot: mapping sensitive fields, redaction options, ephemeral prompt strategies, retention windows, and acceptance criteria for latency/cost. Team agreed on sample workload, pilot timeline, and required artifacts (PII map, anonymized workload, SOC2 docs).
topics: Fallback model policy and cost trade-offs
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining. i think we have about 45 minutes. quick intros?
[00:08] Tom Becker (Clearwave): sure, tom — head of ml at clearwave. we do analytics pipelines for financial data, lots of sensitive fields in prompts.
[00:15] Priya Nambiar (Sec): priya — security lead, i'll be driving the compliance side.
[00:19] Eli Santos (Infra): eli, infra. i'll be doing the bench runs and connecting to our VPC.
[00:24] Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE): hi team, marco from redwood infra, i'll scope the perf tests and redaction options.
[00:29] Lena: great. goal for today: align on success criteria for the PoC, confirm workload size and tokens per request, decide how we handle PII and logs, then agree timeline and next steps. sound right?
[00:40] Tom: yep. high level — we want to validate we can meet p95 latency <= 350ms for our 99th percentile small requests, and ensure any PII is either not logged or redacted. also cost ballpark.
[00:52] Priya: also SOC2 proofs and KMS support. we need audit logs showing who accessed what prompts, but the content of certain fields must be redacted or never persisted.
[01:04] Marco: okay, two parallel requirements: telemetry/auditability vs content minimization. Redwood supports ephemeral prompt options and per-route retention. for the pilot we can propose three telemetry modes: full retention (for debugging), metadata-only (no prompt bodies), and ephemeral (no logs persisted).
[01:22] Eli: can you do sampling? we don't need full retention for production but maybe sample 1% for triage.
[01:27] Marco: yes, sampling is configurable. sampling + field-level redaction before logs hit the platform is safest.
[01:34] Priya: field-level redaction — does Redwood provide a PII detector or do we upload patterns?
[01:38] Marco: both. we have an out-of-the-box regex and ML-based PII detector, but for enterprise we recommend providing a PII mapping file: a CSV with field names, sensitivity level, and redaction policy (hash, redact, token-replace, ephemeral). we'll share a template.
[01:57] Tom: great. our data has nested json blobs — names, account numbers, small attachments. how does redaction handle attachments?
[02:04] Marco: attachments can be scanned via the same pipeline; large binary blobs are hashed and stored externally if needed. during pilot we suggest stripping attachments and replacing with stable hash tokens to simulate payload size without storing content.
[02:18] Lena: let's talk workload sizing — tom, what's your expected RPS and median token length?
[02:22] Tom: peak is ~80 rps for inference calls for one feature, baseline 15 rps sustained. median tokens per request ~220 tokens, but some long requests hit 2k tokens when logs included.
[02:34] Marco: ok that distribution matters — we'll run two bench profiles: short (150-300 tokens) and long tail (1k-2k tokens). target for pilot: p50 latency < 120ms, p95 < 350ms on Dedicated pool, throughput to sustain 80 rps with headroom for bursts to 120 rps for 10 minutes.
[02:53] Eli: we want to test both Dedicated and Hosted fallback to see cost/latency tradeoffs. can Redwood route to fallback models on capacity issues?
[02:59] Marco: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible lighter quantized variant. we'll show latency/cost delta.
[03:05] Priya: retention windows — what's the default? 30 days? and can we enforce shorter for sensitive fields?
[03:10] Marco: hosted default is 30 days for logs, but enterprise/private can set shorter or ephemeral per-route. field-level policies override global retention: e.g., pii_field -> ephemeral.
[03:20] Tom: what's the redaction latency — i mean does redaction add overhead to the request path?
[03:25] Marco: inline redaction can add ~5-15ms depending on complexity; we can also pre-process on customer side to avoid hot path cost. for benchmarking we'll measure with both inline and pre-redaction to see impact.
[03:38] Lena: success criteria in plain terms: (1) performance targets met on our sample workload; (2) PII not persisted beyond agreed retention or redacted/hashed as per policy; (3) cost per 1k tokens approximates agreed range within 20%; (4) audit logs and SSO/KMS integrations validated. any other?
[03:55] Priya: legal asked for proof of deletion during pilot — can you provide deletion logs showing data purged at 24h mark for ephemeral fields?
[04:03] Marco: yes we can show deletion events and audit entries. we'll need the retention matrix to mark which fields are ephemeral.
[04:11] Tom: timeline? we were hoping for a 3-week pilot — 1 week ingest/bench setup, 1 week run, 1 week analysis + run remediations.
[04:19] Lena: that matches Redwood's usual pilot. propose timing: week 1 (12/13-12/19) instrument and upload anonymized sample; week 2 (12/20-12/26) run bench and initial redaction tests; week 3 (12/27-1/2) analysis and final wrap. any blackout dates?
[04:31] Priya: holiday week might be tough but we can still run automated tests — humans will be light.
[04:35] Eli: infra availability fine. we'll provide ephemeral VPC credentials with a lock-down role.
[04:40] Marco: about benchmarks — i'll bring a standard harness that runs 1k-5k requests across token distributions, measuring p50/p95/p99, tail latency, cpu/gpu util, and token cost. for deterministic comparison please provide a stable seed and request set.
[04:56] Tom: we'll anonymize and scrub identifiers and provide 5k requests as a gzip.
[05:00] Lena: security checklist — Priya, what docs do you need?
[05:04] Priya: SOC2 report, data flow diagram, KMS key policies, SSO config, RBAC model, and third-party subprocessor list. also we want to confirm logs are encrypted at rest and in transit.
[05:16] Marco: those are standard; we'll attach our SOC2 summary and provide the KMS integration guide. for encryption at rest we support customer-managed keys in Private mode; hosted mode uses Redwood KMS by default.
[05:28] Tom: any concerns about PHI? we occasionally see health-like attributes in unstructured notes.
[05:33] Marco: same mapping template works. mark those fields as high sensitivity and ephemeral. can you give examples?
[05:38] Tom: patient notes, partial ssn, case IDs.
[05:41] Priya: also need to ensure redaction doesn't break the model output/quality for downstream features. we need to run quality checks against golden prompts.
[05:50] Marco: we'll add quality tests: run prompt set before/after redaction and score via BLEU-ish metrics + human spot checks. accept criteria: less than 5% drop in key-answer extraction accuracy.
[06:03] Lena: okay let's capture the acceptance metrics: latency targets (p95 <= 350ms), throughput (sustain 80 rps), quality delta (<5% accuracy drop), retention enforcement (ephemeral fields deleted within 24h), and demonstrable audit trail.
[06:19] Eli: where do we host the benchmark results?
[06:21] Marco: we'll push to the shared bench sheet and a PDF report in the drive.
[06:25] Tom: any cost estimate for the pilot?
[06:27] Lena: we'll provide a pilot pricing note — usually a small committed spend to reserve dedicated capacity for benching and to cover ephemeral storage costs. i can send an estimate after marco defines the exact instance size used.
[06:38] Priya: about model variants — we prefer to test both a high-accuracy and a quantized lower-cost variant to see the delta.
[06:44] Marco: yes we'll do A/B: same prompts run on redwood-accurate-v1 and redwood-compact-q4. results will show latency, cost per token, and quality metrics.
[06:54] Tom: what's the fallback policy if the dedicated pool reaches capacity in production? we can't have outages.
[06:58] Marco: routing policies can failover to hosted or to a lower-cost variant; also circuit-breakers and rate-limited queuing can help. we'll simulate a capacity event in the bench run.
[07:08] Lena: any legal procurement gating?
[07:11] Priya: standard: DPAs, security questionnaire, indemnities. procurement will kick in if we move beyond pilot.
[07:17] Tom: ok good. one practical Q — can you redact but still give placeholders so downstream features get structure (e.g., replace name with [REDACTED_NAME] vs removing)?
[07:25] Marco: absolutely, policies can replace sensitive tokens with typed placeholders or stable hashes so features that rely on entity alignment still work.
[07:34] Eli: hashing impacts dedup and caches — will that affect KV cache hits?
[07:38] Marco: yes hashed tokens change cache hits, but we can use stable deterministic hashing to preserve alignment across requests. we'll note that in bench analysis.
[07:47] Lena: let's go over immediate next steps and owners. marco, you'll produce the bench script and a short perf config. lena will send PII map template and pilot pricing. tom will upload anonymized 5k workload. priya will share security questionnaire items.
[08:03] Tom: timeline is doable. we'll try to get the sample by end of Tues.
[08:07] Priya: i'll compile the SSO/KMS access list this week.
[08:10] Marco: one more thing — for attachments and long documents we recommend streaming and chunking to reduce peak token cost; we'll test chunking thresholds as part of bench.
[08:20] Tom: noted.
[08:22] Lena: okay final recap — action items in the notes and we'll schedule the benchmark block for next tuesday 12/16 10am-12pm utc?
[08:31] Eli: that works.
[08:33] Priya: yes.
[08:34] Marco: i'll reserve capacity and send calendar invite.
[08:37] Lena: great thank you everyone.
[08:39] End of recording.
